title: Semana Santa
goal: Help make a sawdust carpet before the procession walks over it
culture: Dyed sawdust laid on the road overnight by a whole family, so that the procession can walk straight over it at seven in the morning. The destruction is the point, which does not stop everybody shouting at you not to step on it.

beats.es: (Hay costales de aserrín de colores en media calle.)
beats.objective: Ask what the sawdust is for
beats.good: Aserrín is sawdust, dyed in buckets, and there is a lorry-load of it in the middle of the road.

beats.es: Es para la alfombra. Para la procesión de mañana.
beats.good: A carpet, made of coloured sawdust, laid on the road surface. In the morning the procession walks over it, and that is what it was made for.

beats.en: Sorry. I won’t step on it.
beats.good: No lo pise from her, no lo piso from you. Everybody says it to everybody all night and it is the first thing you will hear when you arrive.

beats.es: Vamos a estar aquí hasta que amanezca.
beats.good: All night, by a whole family, to be walked over at seven in the morning. Saying it back is how you find out that the destruction is the whole idea.
